checks: Verified that the only decoded field change is the explicit mixed-integer maximization domain in the statement, with identical proof bytes. The census and the upper-cover and uniqueness arguments examine exactly all points of that domain. The revised three-fiber statement now names the same domain inside its R×R^d restriction; it still gives the same value at the fixed middle centroid.
Verified source 1d1be0b22c707856 §7, (11), and §§2–3 against the exact source digest. The first-shell reference in §7 is unnecessary for this proof because the integer census is derived directly.

Coordinate flips send q to zero, v to 1_I and p to −1_I. An integer base outside the cube must have coordinate −1, forcing all weight onto p in every convex representation. Cube fibers are exactly T by containment and the assigned generators. Convexity gives the entire product [0,1]^n × T in the hull.

The affine subspace parametrized by z=q+t(v−q) has just the three support sites with t=−1,0,1. An ambient through-point halfspace restricts to a proper through-point cap or the whole subspace. The proper trace pays the frozen triple's bound at its specified middle centroid. The whole trace pays 2V+a. Parallel translation gives the bound for containing halfspaces.

Recomputed the isolation score at p: its terms are 2(k+1)j+(k+1)s−(k−j). With j+s≥1 this is at least (k+1)−k=1. Direct integer enumeration over 86,368 pairs of nonempty I and nonzero w for n=1,…,8 confirmed the identity and inequality, including equality at j=0,s=1.

For a canonical threshold in (0,1], the base penalty of at least two excludes every undesired fiber since its continuous functional is at most one. At q's cap the bonus at p is 2k≥2, so all of A remains included, even at the raised threshold. The own caps at threshold 1/(d+1) cover their simplex fibers and have volume Γ_d V by homothety.

A noncentroid point at q raises one threshold and strictly reduces that own cap. Other cube fibers have isolating caps of mass Γ_d V, and the vertical cap summing over I has only the p fiber of mass a. These strict comparisons use a>0 and Γ_d>0. They apply also at boundary points and for n=1.

The no-addition product has raw maximum Γ_d V by the same isolating canonical caps and the own-fiber centroid lower bound. Dividing by 2^n V+a and subtracting the baseline gives α(2^n−Γ_d)/(2^n(2^n+α)), verifying the derivative.

overlap.comparison: Its compatible three-fiber hypotheses include the n=1 instance, with middle and large endpoint volume V. It gives an existential two-cut lower bound at most [V(2Γ_d−Γ_d²)+a]/2, strictly below Γ_d V+a, and does not provide the binary-core maximum or its uniqueness.

Its reflected-star certificate at (q,g) adds |A∩(2g−T)| to the ordinary simplex centroid depth. Containment in T alone does not force this overlap to equal a. The exact lower and upper bounds and uniqueness here go beyond that certificate.
Its simplex equality case gives the ordinary centroid cap bound used at the no-addition baseline. The one-extra-fiber mixed maximum and uniqueness are outside that ordinary uniform-body result.
